evidence.quote: A referral points the resolver toward them; it is not the final host address.

decisions.reason: Short TTL query costs, overlap and observation, capacity requirements and redundant-server limits support actionable migration/failure decisions without promising instant recovery; DNSSEC never replaces HTTPS.

sourceChecks.claim: Live Cloudflare DNS explanation separates address discovery from later web request; cached answers may avoid resolution. An address does not attest application health.

Live Route53 resolution flow and RFC1034 stub/referral/zone model support recursive authority visits and caching. Reserved .test hierarchy is explicitly illustrative rather than claimed public delegation.
Live Route53 record types confirm A/IPv4, AAAA/IPv6 and CNAME/name. RFC1034 alias processing supports target-record dependency and separately cached records.

Live RFC8767 updates TTL to permit serve-stale after failed refresh; ordinary aging still uses the received lifetime, so a new authoritative TTL does not replace old cached answers. Timeline arithmetic and nonmigration of connections checked.

Live RFC9520 mandates caching resolution failures without asserting absence; linked RFC2308 distinguishes NXDOMAIN/NODATA and gives negative answers their own SOA-derived lifetime. New positive TTL cannot notify an existing negative cache.

Live Route53 failover config uses separate health checks to select DNS answers. Caching means lookup shares cannot guarantee HTTP request shares or instantaneous failover; replacement service capacity remains necessary.

Live RFC1034 establishes resolver/cache, delegation and authority dependencies and alternate server use. Connection/HTTP behavior follows separate protocol stages; repeated identical wrong records do not repair discovery.

Live RFC4033 confirms signed data origin/integrity and trust anchors, explicitly excluding confidentiality and service availability. RFC9525 reference-identity rules preserve the requested source hostname for HTTPS validation rather than substituting a DNS alias.
